description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—as percentages for a “Zero-Shot” evaluation setting, likely from the paper “Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models.” The legend on the right associates colors with categories: teal for N+K+, gold for N−K+, orange for N−K−, and red for N+K−. In the “easy” chart, N+K+ dominates at 55.4%, followed by N−K+ at 38.3%, N−K− at 4.6%, and N+K− at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows N+K+ at 58.8%, N−K+ at 35.4%, N−K− at 4.0%, and N+K− at 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, N−K+ and N−K− are nearly equal at 37.3% and 37.9% respectively, N+K+ drops to 6.7%, and N+K− is 37.3% (though visually a gray bar overlaps this slice, possibly indicating a correction or annotation). The charts are visually aligned horizontally, with percentage values labeled inside each slice, and the “hard” chart includes a gray rectangular overlay on the N+K+ slice, suggesting a possible error or emphasis.
